newsitem.title: UK: Thames Water rises on favourable H1 result.
newsitem.headline: Thames Water rises on favourable H1 result.

text.p: Shares in Thames Water Plc rose 7-1/2 pence to 552-1/2 after the utility hiked its interim dividend by 22 percent and reported first-half profits which were slightly better than most analysts' had expected.
"It's all quite positive," said analyst Daniel Martin at broker BZW.
Thames Water reported pretax profit before exceptional items rose 15 percent to 188 million stg, while market forecasts had centred on 182 million.
The dividend was raised to 11.2 pence per share, while forecasts were for a figure of 10.9 pence.
Shares in the water sector managed to buck a weak market trend with sentiment helped by relatively mild comments from industry watchdog Ofwat.
The regulator suggested water firms show price restraint if they failed to meet investment plans.
The statement coincided with the publication of Ofwat's Report on Financial Performance and Capital Investment.
"The statement could have been a lot more alarmist," said Daniel Martin.
Water firms have been regularly criticised in the British media for not spending enough on maintaining their pipeline networks.

Most other shares in the sector were barely changed in a generally weaker market. Hyder Plc stood out with an 8-1/2 pence gain to 695 although traders said no specific reason was immediately apparent.
